recipes.name: Spooky Calzone Snake
ingredients_raw: 1 cup warm water (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)
0.25 cup grated Parmesan cheese, or to taste
0.5 green bell pepper, cut into strips

steps.text: Dissolve sugar in warm water in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. Sprinkle yeast over water, and let stand for 5 minutes until yeast softens and begins to form a creamy foam. Stir in oil, salt, and 2 cups of flour; mix on Low until the mixture forms a wet dough. With the machine running, add 1 cup of flour, 1/4 cup at a time, and knead until dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl into a ball. Knead for 3 to 5 more minutes, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Lightly oil a large bowl; place dough in the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a towel and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.
Combine ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan cheese, pepperoni, parsley, Italian seasoning, olives, green pepper, and mushrooms in a large bowl; set aside.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Punch down dough; roll it out into a long, flat strip about 9 inches wide by 30 inches long. Spoon filling mixture down the center of dough strip, leaving about 1 inch on all sides for sealing. Pull edges of dough together; pinch to seal and form a long, filled roll. Place roll, seam-side down, onto the parchment paper in a snakey "S" shape, and tuck the ends underneath to seal. Beat egg in a bowl with 1 tablespoon of water; brush egg wash over calzone.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 to 35 minutes, until calzone is golden brown. Let cool for 5 minutes before cutting into individual slices.

raw_recipe.headline: Spooky Calzone Snake
raw_recipe.description: One long calzone, baked in the shape of a snake, can be cut into individual servings after baking. Stuff with your favorite pizza toppings and lots of cheese.

video.description: Watch how to make a slithering snake-shaped calzone. For this video we use a homemade dough that gets rolled out and filled with a mozzarella, ricotta and pepperoni filling. Make it your own by adding your favorite pizza toppings. You'll be excited to make this recipe before a night of trick-or-treating!

review.reviewBody: I submitted this recipe and want to add that I sometimes use pizza dough from the refrigerated section in the store to cut down on time. Then it's a breeze! Add or omit any "pizza toppings" you want to suit your taste. It's great for guests - just omit the colors and shape in a U.

easy to follow recipe. We made it even easier by going to Trader Joe's and picking up some premade pizza dough. lol (The pizza sauce is really good for dipping) Towards the end of baking, I added a second coat of egg wash. Then, the last five minutes I turned oven to broil on low for a little crispy-ness. Finally, I pressed one large garlic clove With about 2 tablespoons of butter and brushed it on :) Really tasty!

I made this lovely snake for a surprise Halloween supper for my husband. It was a "Graveyard Smash," as the song says. Using two Pillsbury canned pizza crusts lessened a lot of time and work, but still kept it very tastey! I used an egg yolk wash with green food coloring, practically smothering the outside. As it baked, it turned a slimily green/gray/brown color. Perfect for grossing out husbands, but probably not so much for kids! We couldn't believe how wonderful this recipe was. Will make often using different shapes and colors for other occasions!

This was a good recipe that could become a great one with a few tweaks. I used Pillsbury's refrigerated pizza dough, added a layer of sauce inside before adding the toppings and used chorizo instead of pepperoni. It was good but the parmesan was overwhelming and made it too salty - next time I'd use 1/3 of what the recipe calls for.

I love this recipe! We don't shape it like a snake though. I did make a few changes though. I always double the recipe. When i proof my yeast i use 1/2 cup of water and when it is time to add it to the flour and other ingredients i use 1 1/2 cups of warm milk (to replace the left out water) In the dough I add 3 cloves of fresh minced garlic, 1-2 tbsp of parsley and 1-2 tbsp Italian seasoning. In the cheese filling I add 2-3 more minced garlic cloves! (we like a lot of garlic) and about 1/2 cup of parm cheese. I like to keep the pepperoni separate from the cheese mixture. I put a thick layer of it on one side of the rolled out dough, then add the cheese mixture and close her up. They are delicious! And if there are any left overs, they taste really good cold the next day too!!!!

I made this for Halloween, I cut pepperoni into diamonds to decorate the back, used a sliver piece for the tongue, and green pimento olives sliced in half for the eyes. I also pulled the face end upward and curled it over to make room for olives to set
in and to make nostrils. It came out scary good. I'll try to post a picture later.

Great idea! I used store bought frozen pizza dough, thawed overnight. Also I added a layer of pizza sauce before adding the filling, which ended up making the marinara dipping sauce redundant. It was beautiful and the kids loved it, though there was some fighting over the snake’s head!

It got eatten so fast that I forgot to take a photo. Will need to make again. I was debating, why bother since it's like a pizza, but not really with the ricotta cheese instead of tomato sauce. I made it with chopped anchovies near the head for people who prefer them to salami and with salami instead of pepperoni the rest of the way. It was a great hit with the kids and adults. I baked it at 450 for 20 minutes and it was nice and crisp on the outside and chewy and soft inside with the cheese well melted. I also added an egg to the cheese mixture. Will definitely make again.

Tremendous fun to make & eat. I cheated & used a can of crescent roll for the dough (pinched together seams), then simply put a light layer of spaghetti sauce, followed by a single layer of turkey pepperoni & a generous sprinkling of shredded mozzarella. Used pastry brush to add diluted yellow food coloring to dough, then used diluted green food coloring to add spots & lines, dabbing gently with a paper towel to ensure green did not run. Even my incredibly picky daughter (who never eats) finished all her "Snake" AND salad (that is a huge compliment for me!). Great concept that can be made more easily using pre-made ingredients...great time-saver & inexpensive meal for a busy weeknight...have fun with this one!
I added 15 ozs of ricotta instead of a cup. Served it with marinara sauce for dipping. Everyone loved it!
I added mushrooms and other veggies, which ultimately made the interior toppings too big, so my scary snake turned out to be an ugly eel, but everyone loved the taste!
This was so cute! The dough was very easy to work with, and I made it exactly according to the recipe.
Was the best Halloween meal ever!
Fun and tasty treat for Halloween
It worked out really well. Was tasty and looked great on the Halloween party table!
family enjoys this every Halloween. Used 2 rolls refrigerator pizza crust. Can adjust the ingredients to your liking.

Overall, these calzones were good. I left out the mushrooms and olives, though. The dough for this recipe is quite good. It would be good for pizza crust or breadsticks. I kneaded with my hands, let rise for an hour, kneaded a second time and let rise for 2 more hours. Also, I didn't attempt the snake shape. I rolled out my dough and cut it in half to make 2 triangle calzones. They were huge, so make 4 at the least.
Absolutely delicious. Will definitely make it again
Excellent! Everyone in my office loved this meal. I did lower the amount of cheese a bit, and it still turned out great.
